## VSiN on this hire — The Coaching Carousel Never Stops

*Adam Burke, p. 29. GUIDE CONTENT — TTW reference notes summarising the guide's assessment; the judgement is the guide's.*

Adam Burke opens by placing himself: he would not call himself a glass-half-full person by nature, but when it comes to new coaching hires he is often optimistic — and he cannot say that about North Texas's hire of Brown, who was let go from West Virginia in 2024 and served as Steve Sarkisian's assistant in 2025. He gives the record fairly: over 120 games of head coaching experience, all at the FBS level, and real success at Troy with three 10-win seasons in a row before heading to Morgantown. He then draws the stylistic contrast that matters here — Brown is an offensive-minded guy, but not like Eric Morris, who ran more of a run-and-shoot style. His conclusion is hedged but clear: it might work and the bar isn't terribly high, given the programme has three winning seasons since 2013, but it feels like UNT is drifting closer to mediocrity again rather than living up to what should be their new standard.
